text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Sunday will be the first day of the Eid al-Fitr feast in Egypt, marking the end of the fasting month of Ramadan. At the armed forces mosque, President Hosni Mubarak performs the last Friday prayers of Ramadan, and conveys to Arab leaders his Eid greetings.
- Sudan prevents Middle East News Agency journalist from leaving Khartoum. He is questioned about his reports.
- Preparations made at Cairo airport to receive up to a quarter of a million travellers as Eid al-Fitr approaches.
- 100 mosques will be built in Britain by the end of the century, supported by donations made by Moslems there.
- Birth certificates approved for two brothers who had a gender-change operation.
- Egypt's finance minister is released from the hospital.
